clue.text: Party trick: minister keeping tax as priority

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick

indicators.note: keeping says one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: to minister is to serve
VAT is value added tax
a top priority is number one, the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A party's clever ploy: a government minister putting tax at the top of the agenda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as priority' reads as a phrase about policy, but a top priority is number one, I, which joins VAT inside the minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The Conservative Party is one of Britain's two main political parties.

clue.text: Pet hate starts with poetry — hence the electrons

parts.note: a cat is a typical pet

indicators.note: starts says to take only the first letter of hate

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A pet's loathing of verse, with a leap to electrons.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrons flow out of the cathode, the electrode where current leaves a device.

clue.text: Granny's very partial to this cloth

parts.note: nan is an informal word for grandmother
to be keen on something is to be very partial to it

explanation.surface: Grandmother is especially fond of this fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth originally made in Nanjing.

clue.text: Interval entailed partaking of a meal of lentils

indicators.note: partaking of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A break in proceedings involved sharing a lentil dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ervalenta was a Victorian invalid food made from ground lentils.

clue.text: Struggles to contain black feelings

indicators.note: to contain says one piece is held inside another

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Inner battles holding down dark emotions.
explanation.definitionFit: Vibes is informal for vibrations, the feelings or atmosphere sensed from a person or place.

clue.text: Terracotta horse in house that went with the wind

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside another

parts.words: house that went with the wind
parts.note: Tara is the plantation house in Gone with the Wind
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A clay horse stands in the mansion from Gone with the Wind.
explanation.walkthrough: TARA is the O'Hara family home in the novel and film Gone with the Wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanagra figurines are small terracotta statuettes from ancient Greece.

clue.text: Unbalanced state of 13 before I leave

parts.note: 13 across is green, which is vert in French and in heraldry
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Feeling giddy and green, I should leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 across is GREEN; heraldry calls green VERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertigo is dizziness, a state of feeling off balance.

clue.text: Gaea's change of heart over the 13 engine?

definitions.note: Gaea is the Greek goddess of the earth; read as Gaea is

indicators.note: over here means in place of, so one word stands instead of another

parts.note: 13 across is green, and the Green Goddess was the army fire engine
rearranging the letters of heart, a change to it, gives the planet's name

explanation.surface: The earth mother has a change of heart about the green fire engine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Green Goddess was the army fire engine used in British strikes. Rearranged, HEART gives EARTH, which replaces GREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaea, or Gaia, is the primordial goddess of the earth in Greek myth.

clue.text: Insect maybe flying on and off, reported flying in Russia

parts.note: an ant is an example of an insect, and some do fly

indicators.note: reported signals that a word is to be taken by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: the word off, as pronounced, matches the Russian surname ending -ov

explanation.surface: An insect zipping back and forth, apparently airborne over Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' turns OFF into the sound-alike OV, the common ending of Russian surnames.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonov is the maker of Soviet and Russian aircraft, so its planes are flying in Russia.

clue.text: Mars' hill, place of pilgrimage once

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for a mountain or hill
Ares is the Greek counterpart of the Roman war god Mars

explanation.surface: The Areopagus, Mars' hill in Athens, was once a place people journeyed to.
explanation.walkthrough: Mars' hill suggests the Areopagus in Athens, but it is split: the god Ares and a ben.
explanation.definitionFit: Benares is the former name of Varanasi, the holy Hindu city on the Ganges visited by pilgrims.

clue.text: Star performer wanting to fly? Ride horse

indicators.note: wanting to suggests the letters are eager to move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A celebrity longs to take wing, but is told to ride a horse instead.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange FLY RIDE HORSE. 'Star performer' sounds like a celebrity, but means an astronomer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Fred Hoyle was a famous astronomer, a performer in the study of stars.

clue.text: How Othello loved to be in debt, having interrupted payment

indicators.note: having interrupted says one piece breaks into the middle of another

parts.note: a toll is a charge paid for using a road or bridge
to owe is to be in debt

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean reflection on love and money: Othello's affections and a debt that cut into a payment.
explanation.walkthrough: Othello's dying speech says he 'loved not wisely but too well'.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello describes himself as one that loved not wisely but excessively, the quoted phrase.

clue.text: Shakespearean gentleman to indicate return of French king

parts.note: to sign is to indicate or signal

indicators.note: return of says the following word is read backwards

parts.note: roi is French for king

explanation.surface: A gentleman from Shakespeare signals that the French monarch is coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: Signior is the Elizabethan form of the Italian title for a gentleman, used often in Shakespeare.

clue.text: New party? …

definitions.meaning: the ... Party is a political party

explanation.definitionFit: Green means fresh or untried, and the Greens are an environmentalist political party.

clue.text: … likewise, in lieu, the person next door to Spooner

definitions.note: likewise means the definition is the same as the previous clue's: a new party

indicators.note: to Spooner signals swapping the opening sounds of two words, as Dr Spooner was said to do

parts.note: taken as written
a neighbour is the person living next door

explanation.surface: The trailing dots continue the previous clue: in place of a new party, the neighbour as Spooner would say it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'likewise' borrows the previous clue: another New party. Swap the opening sounds of LIEU and NEIGHBOUR to hear 'new labour'.
explanation.definitionFit: New Labour was the rebranded Labour Party of the Blair years, a new party as in the previous clue.

clue.text: Reveller, the fool, interrupting mourner

indicators.note: interrupting says one piece breaks into another

parts.note: a wailer laments loudly, as a mourner
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A party-goer, being an idiot, barges into a grieving person.
explanation.definitionFit: A wassailer is someone who goes wassailing, drinking and carousing in festivity.

clue.text: See 25
Macbeth, questioning his title, is inflammable

definitions.note: an adjective here defining a noun: the gas is described by what it is

parts.note: Macbeth would refer to himself as me
Macbeth was Thane of Glamis and Cawdor

explanation.surface: Macbeth, doubting he is truly thane, is a hothead.
explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth, hailed by the witches, might ask 'Me, thane?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane is a highly flammable gas, the main component of natural gas.

clue.text: Passed being a passenger?

definitions.meaning: a motion that passes a vote is said to be ...
a passenger is conveyed or transported

explanation.definitionFit: A motion carried is passed, and a passenger is someone carried in a vehicle.

clue.text: Identity card opens admittance into games for rum rum party …

indicators.note: admittance into says some letters are let inside another set of letters

parts.note: games or sport is play

indicators.note: the second rum, meaning odd or strange, says the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
ID is short for identity

indicators.note: opens says only the first letter of card is used

explanation.surface: Showing an ID card to get into the games for some sort of rum party.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'rum' (odd) is the anagram signal; PLAY and RUM mix to PLAYMRU, and 'admittance into' places ID and C after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaid Cymru is the Welsh nationalist political party.

clue.text: Prince likely to be open to persuasion

parts.note: liable means likely, as in liable to happen

explanation.surface: A royal is probably susceptible to being talked round.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliable means easily influenced, flexible in opinion.

clue.text: Times following removal of leader from Egyptian states

indicators.note: following says this piece comes after the other
removal of leader says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: Nasser was the Egyptian president
T is the abbreviation for time, so TS is times

explanation.surface: Removing the head of an Egyptian state, in times past.
explanation.walkthrough: Gamal Abdel Nasser led Egypt from 1954 to 1970; dropping his N leaves ASSER.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert is to state firmly, so asserts means states.

clue.text: … its openings gain admittance before there's fever inside

parts.note: to enter is to gain admittance
its refers back to the identity card of the previous clue, whose first letters are I and C

explanation.surface: A continuation: the card's initials get you in before a fever takes hold internally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its' refers back to the 'Identity card' of 19 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Enteric fever is typhoid, an infection of the intestines, so it is a fever inside the body.

clue.text: See 19 across
Nobleman shortly entertaining love poet

indicators.note: entertaining means holding something within, as a host holds guests

parts.note: an aristo is an aristocrat, the word shortened
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: An aristocrat host welcomes a romantic poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludovico Ariosto was the Italian Renaissance poet who wrote Orlando Furioso.

clue.text: Am I dust? Hardly, though I might include a dirt track

definitions.text: I might include a dirt track

indicators.note: hardly signals that the words are not to be read as they stand but rearranged

explanation.surface: A musing on mortality, answered by a sports ground claiming it might have a dirt track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardly' says 'Am I dust' is not to be taken as it stands, so rearrange its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports arena may contain a cinder or dirt track for racing, such as speedway.

clue.text: Ballots carried me out from party

indicators.note: out signals the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A party member boasts that the votes carried them out of the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' says the letters of BALLOTS CARRIED ME are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Liberal Democrats are a British political party formed in 1988.

clue.text: Leaders have embraced mercy — perhaps in the battlebus

indicators.note: have embraced says one piece is held inside another

parts.note: heads are leaders
quarter is mercy shown to a defeated enemy, as in 'give no quarter'

explanation.surface: Party leaders have shown clemency while touring on the campaign bus.
explanation.walkthrough: A battlebus is a party's campaign coach in a British election.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaign battlebus may serve as a mobile base or command centre for the party.
